title: Object response patterns across two image variation levels aligned more in IT than V4 in one of two macaques
abstract: We tested whether a greater object variance share in macaque IT includes retention of object response patterns across image variation. We used the public MajajHong2015 assembly, with 64 objects at fixed and varied views. Disjoint images estimate signal energies for a cross-set cosine, without a fitted map. In Chabo, with 30 sites per area, alignment after category mean removal rose from 0.407 in V4 to 0.650 in IT. The difference was 0.243, with a sampling spread of 0.142 to 0.344. The spectral decay difference was uncertain: -0.027, with a spread of -0.308 to 0.255. In Tito, with 16 sites per area, the identity alignment difference was uncertain: 0.051, with a spread of -0.054 to 0.156. Within-category label shuffles removed identity alignment. Additional trial-SD scaling gave similar results, but the assembly was already standardized. Thus Chabo extends the earlier class-share result to stable object patterns without a resolved spectral increase. The second animal did not clearly replicate the alignment increase. Spreads describe 200 site selections and image partitions, not uncertainty across animals or new objects. Independent image and noise assumptions, joint image changes, small site samples and one response window limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Cross-set object alignment, alignment after category mean removal, and spectral decay in V4 and IT. Error bars show mean plus or minus 1.96 SD over site selections and image partitions. They are not animal confidence intervals.
